name: Spitting
overview: Scripture presents spitting primarily as an act of indignity and shame, as seen when it is done in the face to express contempt or punishment, such as in Numbers 12:14 and Deuteronomy 25:9. Job laments being spat upon as a sign of deep rejection (Job 30:10), and Jesus Himself endured spitting during His suffering (Matthew 26:67; 27:30), highlighting the depth of human cruelty He bore. Yet, spitting also appears in a healing context, as Jesus used spittle in miraculous acts (Mark 7:33), demonstrating His sovereign power to restore and heal even through what might seem a humble or offensive means.
